sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 of the August 1929 Sanborn atlas of Berlin, New Jersey, covering the southwestern edge of West Berlin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The upper part shows the blocks between Heights Avenue and Ivins Avenue on either side of the White Horse Pike: Egg Harbor Road, Park Avenue, Dill Avenue, Clementon Road and Kerhart Avenue on the west, and Atlantic Avenue, Hudson Avenue and Haddon Avenue on the east, where Atlantic Avenue runs beside the railroad on both sides of the tracks. Development is light: scattered frame dwellings, a few stores, auto repairing and garage buildings, gasoline tanks, Marigold Gardens on Clementon Road, an oil reclaiming plant off Kerhart Avenue and a cemetery house by the cemetery west of Egg Harbor Road. The lower half of the sheet is almost empty: the White Horse Pike continues south past the Rendezvous Hotel, a garage and a few dwellings, the railroad runs down the east side, the dashed drives of Camden County Park curve across the southwest, and Fairfax Avenue is sketched at the east edge with the outline of sheet 10. The west margin is marked no exposure. Sheet numbers 9, 10 and 12 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Control lies only in the upper half (Heights Avenue to Kerhart Avenue); the lower half with Camden County Park and the southern White Horse Pike is placed by extrapolation and is less certain.
The modern Clementon Road / West White Horse Pike junction falls about 50 m north of where the drawn Atlantic Avenue meets the White Horse Pike, so it was not used.
White Horse Pike is West White Horse Pike in OpenStreetMap; Ivins Av. is not in OpenStreetMap.

Map. Berlin series sheet 11 (West Berlin), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper right. Heights Av (top) to the White Horse Pike and Camden County Park; Egg Harbor Rd, Park Av, Dill Av, Clementon Rd, Kerhart Av, Ivins Av, Hudson and Haddon Avs; the Atlantic City railroad with Atlantic Av along it. One part.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 of the August 1929 Sanborn atlas of Berlin, New Jersey, covering the centre of West Berlin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The sheet runs from Laurel Avenue and Bates Avenue at the top to Heights Avenue at the bottom, and from Egg Harbor Road and the White Horse Pike on the west to Haddon Avenue on the east. The railroad, lettered W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.), crosses from top to bottom with Atlantic Avenue on both sides and the West Berlin station beside it. West of the tracks are Union Avenue, Park Avenue, Fairview Avenue (not open) and Elm Avenue, a coal yard, and the woodworking, finishing, machine shop and foundry buildings of the Baccellieri Bros. Mfg. Co. East of the tracks a grid of Stokes, Dayton, Pine, Chestnut, Warren and Hudson Avenues is crossed by Bates, Walnut, Bethel, Fairview, Elm and Heights Avenues. The area is mostly frame dwellings on large lots with a public school and its heating plant on Bates Avenue, a garment factory and stores along Haddon Avenue, a church and a Baptist mission. The west margin is marked no exposure and a cemetery lies beyond the White Horse Pike.
notes: Renamed since (OpenStreetMap): Bates Av. is Bate Avenue; Dayton Av. is North Avenue; Chestnut Av. east of the railroad is Chester Avenue; Fairview Av. east of the railroad is Lucas Avenue; Elm Av. east of the railroad is Patton Avenue; White Horse Pike is West White Horse Pike.
Atlantic Avenue on both sides of the railroad was left out of the control: the detector paired rail and street lines there.
Elm Avenue / Park Avenue fits 15 m off and was excluded; Park Avenue west of the railroad appears realigned.
The railroad is lettered W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.); OpenStreetMap names it the Atlantic City Line.

Map. Berlin series sheet 12 (West Berlin), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper right. Bates Av to Heights Av, Egg Harbor Rd to Haddon Av; Union, Fairview, Elm, Bethel, Walnut Avs, Dayton, Pine, Chestnut, Warren, Hudson Avs; railroad with Atlantic Av on both sides; Baccellieri Bros Mfg Co, public school. One part.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 of the August 1929 Sanborn atlas of Berlin, New Jersey, covering the northwestern part of West Berlin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north up. The sheet runs from Acton Road and Clifton Avenue at the top to the White Horse Pike at the bottom, and from Stoughton Avenue on the west to Brill Avenue on the east. Franklin Avenue crosses the sheet from north to south, bending where it crosses the railroad, lettered W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.), which runs east-west across the middle. South of the railroad Egg Harbor Road runs southeast, with Chestnut Avenue (Vine), Locust Avenue, Laurel Avenue, Park Avenue and Atlantic Avenue near it, and Union Avenue, Berwick, Maylan and Stoughton Avenues and Cedar Avenue lead toward the pike. The area is thinly built: frame dwellings and coops, poultry houses on the large lots north of the railroad, the C. W. Wolf Inc. meat distributors and the Garden Inn on the south side of the pike, and the Berlin Inn at Brill Avenue. Several streets on the west side are marked not open, and the north edge carries the arbitrary line of Acton Road. Sheet numbers 12 and 14 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Renamed since (OpenStreetMap): Maylan Av. is Malan Avenue; Acton Rd. appears to be Plymouth Avenue; Union Av. east of Franklin Avenue is Maple Avenue; Cedar Av. is North Cedar Avenue; Brill Av. is North Brill Avenue; White Horse Pike is West White Horse Pike; Franklin Av. south of Egg Harbor Road is North Franklin Avenue.
Modern Franklin Avenue runs straight where the drawn street bends at the railroad.
Egg Harbor Road / Maple Avenue / Union Avenue fits about 8 m off and was excluded; the modern junction has been rebuilt.
Berwick and Stoughton Avenues are not in OpenStreetMap.

Map. Berlin series sheet 13 (West Berlin), 100 ft to an inch, north up. Acton Rd and Clifton Av to the White Horse Pike, Stoughton Av to Brill Av; Franklin, Chestnut (Vine), Locust, Union, Laurel, Cedar Avs, Egg Harbor Rd; W.J.&S.R.R. (P.R.R.) crossing. One part.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 of the August 1929 Sanborn atlas of Berlin, New Jersey, covering the northern part of West Berlin, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north toward the upper right. The sheet runs from the large undivided blocks above Washington Avenue at the top to Bates Avenue at the bottom, and from Arch Avenue and Hudson (Pine) Avenue on the west to 3rd Avenue on the east. Cross streets are Washington, Lincoln, McClellan, Franklin, Clarence and Grant Avenues; north-south streets are Hampton (not open), Green, French, North, Pine, Bishop and Haddon Avenues and 1st, 2nd and 3rd Avenues, with Krumm Avenue and Center Avenue running diagonally. Haddon Avenue is the main street, with stores, a post office, an auto repair shop and the fire department engine house; the Lone Star Laundry stands on Lincoln Avenue and a standpipe near Green Avenue. Elsewhere the blocks hold frame dwellings, many with small sheds and coops, and the Wesley M.E. Church faces Bates Avenue. Large parts of the eastern blocks are still vacant lots. Sheet numbers 12 and 13 mark the adjoining sheets.
notes: Renamed since (OpenStreetMap): Washington Av. is Boyer Avenue; Lincoln Av. east of Green Avenue is Lester Avenue; Bates Av. is Bate Avenue.
Hudson (Pine) Av. and Pine Av. were left out of the control: their junctions fit 4 to 16 m off, so the modern Pine Avenue is not on the old line.
1st Avenue / Clarence Avenue was excluded (detected 14 m off).
Green, French, Hampton and Center Avenues are not in OpenStreetMap.

Map. Berlin series sheet 14 (West Berlin), 100 ft to an inch, north to the upper right. Washington Av to Bates Av, Hudson (Pine) Av to 3rd Av; Lincoln, McClellan, Franklin, Clarence, Grant, Center Avs, North, Pine, Bishop, Haddon, 1st, 2nd Avs. One part.
